# glyfp <a href="#documentation"><img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="138" alt="glyfp logo" /></a>

The glyfp package represents glycans as fingerprints for comparison and modeling.
It provides binary and count fingerprints of connected glycan substructures,
reusable encoders for multiple batches, and optional pretrained SweetNet embeddings.
Inputs can be glyrepr structures or text in formats supported by glyparse.

## Installation

glyfp is under local development and is not yet available from CRAN, R-universe,
or a remote repository. Install it from this package directory:

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::repo_add(glycoverse = "https://glycoverse.r-universe.dev")
pak::local_install(".")
```

**Note:** Tips and troubleshooting for the meta-package
[glycoverse](https://github.com/glycoverse/glycoverse) also apply here:
[Installation of glycoverse](https://github.com/glycoverse/glycoverse#installation).

## Documentation

- 🚀 Get started: [Comparable glycan fingerprints](vignettes/fingerprints.Rmd)
- 📚 Reference: [Fingerprint functions and encoders](man/glycan_fingerprint.Rd)
- 🧠 Pretrained embeddings: [SweetNet](vignettes/sweetnet.Rmd)

These links point to the local source documentation until the package website is
published. After installation, use `help("glycan_fingerprint", package = "glyfp")`
and `browseVignettes("glyfp")`.

## Role in `glycoverse`

glyfp is being developed as part of the
[Glycoverse ecosystem](https://github.com/glycoverse/glycoverse). It builds on
glyrepr for glycan structures, glyparse for text parsing, and glymotif for
substructure extraction and counting. Its fingerprints are intended as inputs
to glycan comparison, clustering, and predictive workflows.

## Example

```{r}
library(glyfp)
```

Encode a batch of glycans as substructure counts:

```{r}
glycans <- c("Gal(b1-3)Gal(b1-3)Gal(b1-", "Gal(b1-")
glycan_fingerprint(glycans, method = "substructure_count", max_size = 2)
```

The repeated disaccharide is counted twice, including overlapping occurrences.
Use `method = "substructure_binary"`, the default, for presence/absence.

For multiple batches, fit once and reuse the encoder:

```{r}
encoder <- fit_fingerprint(glycans, method = "substructure_binary")
transform_fingerprint(c("Gal(b1-3)Gal(b1-", NA_character_), encoder)
```

Each top-level substructure call fits its own dictionary; independently fitted
batches are not directly comparable, even when their vectors have equal lengths.
The [getting-started vignette](vignettes/fingerprints.Rmd) shows both combining
batches in one call and reusing an encoder, along with missing and unknown input.
